To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frl operons of E. coli encode an unusual Amadori aldolase that catalyses the metal dependent reversible interconversion of the Amadori compounds fructoselyine and psicoselysines.

the frl operons encode three enzymes involved in the degradation of the unusual Amadore compound fructoselynine, that fructoselyne can be interconverted to psicoselysime and back by a metal dependent epimerase and that the frlA gene encodes an ABC-type transporter.
a third enzyme is required to metabolize the unusual Amadoris compound psicoselysin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the enzymology and physiological significance of fructosamine metabolism in Escherichiacoli.
the characterization of a novel enzyme, fructoselysin 3-epi-merase, which catalyses an epimerization reaction at C-3 of an Amadori compound.
the elucidation of the metabolic pathways involved in the utilization of unusual Amadori compounds by microorganisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fructoselysin 3-epimerae (FrlC) is the enzyme that interconverts the two Amadori compounds fructoselyine (FL) and psicoselyine (PL), both of which are present in E. coli.
the frl operone encodes the enzymes required for the metabolism of fructosyllysine and psicosyllysine.
fructoselysin 3-epimerae is a novel enzyme, involved in the metabolism in E. coli of fructoselynse and psicoselysines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E. coli has developed a complex pathway for the metabolism of fructosamine, the most abundant Amadori compound present in Nature, which is formed by the condensation of lysine and glucose.
E. coli can use fructoselysin as a source of lysine and glucose, and psicoselysines can be used as a source of glucose and lysine, but not as a source of carbon and nitrogen.
fructosely- and psicoselysines are metabolized by the same enzymes in E. coli, and that the frl operons are involved in the metabolism both compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fructoselyine 3- epimerase is an enzyme with a new function, the reversible interconversion between fructoselysin and its C-3 psicoselysines.
fructoselysin 3-epimease is an enzyme involved in Amadori compound metabolism.

E. coli has developed an efficient system to metabolize fructoselysin and psicoselysines, the C-3 and C-6 epimers of the classical Amadori compound fructoselycine, and that the latter is the only one that can be used for growth.
